text:
incident-bot: [PD] SEV3: gpu-ecc-errors spike on pool-gpu-4 - alert fired 1774509999
Irene: ack - I'm oncall for the hour, switching to incident channel.
Samir: on it. what did the alert include?
Irene: message: 'gpu_ecc_errors_total rate > 0.02 over 5m for node=pool-gpu-4'
Maria: pinged for handoff if you need escalation.
opsbot: mitigation suggestion: mark node Unscheduable + live-migrate pods if possible.
Josh: quick check - any pod evictions or OOMs around that time?
Samir: logs show increased ECC corrections on node, but no OOMs. A few long-running batch pods had tail latency spikes.
Irene: running quick PromQL to verify spread:
```
sum by(node)(rate(gpu_ecc_errors_total[5m]))
```
Samir: result: pool-gpu-4 at ~0.035, nearest node pool-gpu-7 at 0.003. Looks localized.
Irene: any customer-facing errors?
Josh: Slack search + error dashboard - one customer (acct: red-cap-42) reported inference failures at 02:41 UTC. correlating with ECC spike window. Possible soft errors causing retries.
Maria: ok, that means potential customer impact, escalate to SEV2 if we see retries causing 5xx. Current evidence is limited -> keep SEV3 but notify relevant CEs.
PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by Irene (oncall). Handoff ETA if needed: 03:15 UTC to Maria.
Irene: short-term mitigation - cordon + drain node to avoid further tail anomalies. I'll run cordon then live-migrate non-daemonset pods.
opsbot: running: `kubectl cordon node/pool-gpu-4` (simulated)
Irene: cordoned. starting drain with `kubectl drain node/pool-gpu-4 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
Samir: hold on drain - some high-memory jobs pinned to node, we should evict safely. I'll move lowest-priority pods first.
Irene: agreed, doing progressive eviction, will keep node up for diagnostics until pods moved.
Josh: while we move pods, let's mute the alert to avoid noise during action – change alert to suppress for 30m.
Samir: changing temporary alerting rule in Alertmanager: silence `gpu_ecc_errors_spike` for 30m with note "in-progress node drain".
Irene: silence in place :thumbsup:
Maria: capture of immediate actions: cordon -> progressive drain -> silence alert -> monitor downstream effects.
Samir: observed ECC error rate dropping to 0.004 after evacuation; tail latency for batch jobs trending back to baseline.
Irene: good. initiate health check on node: nvme SMART, dmesg for ECC/PCIe messages, and vendor telemetry upload.
Josh: copying relevant commands:
```
journalctl -k -u nvidia-driver -n 200 --no-pager | grep -i ecc
nvidia-smi -q -d ECC
```
Samir: dmesg shows repeated ECC correction events, no unrecoverable errors yet. Recommend replacing DIMM/gpu hardware for that node in maintenance window.
Maria: create follow-up ticket for hardware swap (ENGINFRA-3342). assign to eng-infra and mark as P2.
Irene: noted. Also recommending alert tuning: current rule triggers on raw rate > 0.02 which catches transient spikes. Proposal in thread: move to rolling 30m rate with threshold 0.015 and add cardinality (>=2 nodes) to avoid single-node noise.
Samir: alternative: keep 5m rate but require 3 occurrences within 15m (for flapping suppression). Both work.
Josh: also add metric-based gating for customer impact: only page on ECC spikes when there is correlated increase in pod restarts or inference 5xxs.
Irene: agreed. Action items for post-incident:
- create dashboard panel for `sum(rate(gpu_ecc_errors_total[5m])) by (node)` with alert overlay
- add replication panel for `gpu_memory_used_bytes` and `gpu_utilization` to correlate load
- update alert rule to either 30m rolling rate or "3x occurrences in 15m" + require >1 node affected
- add runbook section: progressive drain, how to check vendor telemetry, how to file hardware RMA
Maria: I'll own the dashboard and runbook updates, will drop link when ready.
Irene: handoff note for Maria at 03:15 UTC: node cordoned, drain complete, silence still active until 03:10 UTC, hardware ticket created, customer contacted by Josh.
Maria: picked up handoff. I'll follow up with eng-infra to schedule DIMM/GPU replacement and implement alert tuning tomorrow morning.
Samir: small config snippet for the alert proposal (Prometheus rule YAML):
```
- alert: GPUECCSpike
  expr: sum by(node)(rate(gpu_ecc_errors_total[30m])) > 0.015
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "GPU ECC spike on {{ $labels.node }}"
```
Irene: add note to require `count_nodes_with_alert >= 2` in the orchestration layer or set severity lower if single-node.
Josh: customer update prepared: "We saw transient ECC corrections on one GPU node which caused retries for some inference requests. We've evacuated the node and scheduled hardware replacement; no long-term data loss expected." will send after Maria confirms hardware ticket.
opsbot: automated post-incident checklist added to thread.
Maria: posting dashboard draft: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/gpu-health/pool-gpu-ecctrends (will populate panels)
Irene: thanks team. closing active mitigation. leaving a follow-up to verify hardware swap and alert tuning next business day.
Samir: re-open if recurrence. :white_check_mark:
